packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-03 - unverified image reading (reader C)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification or prior reading of this material was in my context. This is a blind reading.
- Beyond the brief: to cut through the brown staining I made local derivative copies of the packet images
  (red channel, contrast stretch, and half-tile crops enlarged) with a small PIL script in my scratchpad.
  All readings below are from the supplied images or those derivatives; no other file, catalogue,
  edition, web or search tool was used. packet.json was not opened.

OVERALL VERDICT
- This packet is at the limit of legibility for me. The script is a small, very cursive late-medieval
  hand in faint grey-brown ink, on paper heavily foxed and water-stained, with losses at edges.
  I could fix only isolated words and letter-groups; I could NOT produce connected spans of ten or
  more secure lines on any face. What follows is honest letter-level reading with heavy query marks.
  Treat almost every word as uncertain. Gaps marked [illegible] reflect what I could not resolve after
  enlarged and enhanced views, not lack of looking.
- Recommend: multispectral / UV images, or higher-contrast native scans, before anyone relies on this
  for a source match.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
Four faces appear in the packet:
- Face A: image-001 overview (small landscape strip, c. 13.5 x 8 cm visible against ruler), tiles 002 (left)
  and 003 (right). Two columns of writing occupy only the upper half; lower half blank (probably a
  lower margin, or the strip is a cut-down binding fragment). About 12-13 lines per column survive.
  Top edge torn; first line damaged. Right column has a dark modern-looking ink blot near top right
  and a black curved stroke in the right margin (prob. later mark or damage).
- Face B: image-004 overview (same strip, other side, appears inverted relative to A), tiles 005 (left)
  and 006 (right). Two columns, c. 10-12 lines each, upper half only. Ruled frame lines faintly visible
  (horizontal ruling line under col. a line 10). At the far left edge (005) there is text written
  vertically (rotated 90 degrees) along the margin - probably from another use of the sheet or a
  binding pastedown; not read.
- Face C: image-007 overview (portrait leaf c. 14 x 20 cm), tiles 008-013 (2 x 3 grid, left/right,
  top/middle/bottom, overlapping). Two columns, c. 40+ lines each, very faint. The left column is
  almost entirely lost under staining in 008/010; the right column (009, 011, 013) is somewhat better.
  In col. b near the top (009) there is a ruled/underlined line and two indented lines that look set
  off from the surrounding prose (possibly a quotation or heading - observation only).
- Face D: image-014 overview (portrait leaf, other side of C), tiles 015-020. Two columns, c. 45 lines,
  same hand. Upper parts of both columns more legible than C.
- No rubrics, no enlarged coloured initials, no running titles visible in any face. Some letters
  have enlarged cadels at line starts. No interlinear glosses identified.
- Tentative interpretation (not identification): continuous prose, apparently devotional/theological
  vocabulary (anima, gaudium, passio, gratia, misericordia, deus/dominus) recurs.

SELECTED SPANS
Below, "L" numbers count lines of writing from the top of the named image. Overlapping tiles repeat
lines; I note overlaps rather than count twice. Abbreviations expanded in ( ); ? before an uncertain
reading.

- Face C col. a upper and middle (008, 010): ink largely lost under staining; nothing secure.
- Face D lower halves (017-020): viewed only via the overview; not transcribed.
- Vertical marginal text on Face B (005 left edge): not read.

LIMITATIONS
- Nearly every word above is queried. Do not use any single reading as a search anchor without
  re-checking; the most stable-looking items are 009 L4 "odiui(?) et iam", 009 L15/011 L3
  "gaudium", 016 L7 "magister(?)", and 002 L4 ending "-pla".
- Column order and recto/verso order are not established; the two small strips (A/B) may be
  inverted relative to each other.
- A wider/better-lit or multispectral capture is needed for a usable reading.
